blurb:
The shelter staff tried to get a handle on this guy when he first came in. He had other plans. That's how a 49-pound Shepherd/Rottweiler mix earned the name Mr. Worldwide, and honestly it fits.

He's three years old, moderately active, and the kind of dog who needs a little patience up front before he really opens up. The staff put it plainly: take things slow with him first, then branch out to the outdoor adventures. Hiking, long walks, something with movement and purpose. He's going to thrive with a family that likes doing stuff outside.

He's picky about other dogs, so a home where he's the only dog is probably the better fit. His history with kids is unknown since he came in without much background, so families with young children should call ahead and ask about a meet. He's vaccinated, microchipped, heartworm negative, and already neutered.

Lewisville Animal Services is on College Pkwy in Lewisville. Walk in during visiting hours to meet him.

scoring_notes:
• The name origin story alone is newsletter gold and gives editors a natural, memorable headline hook
• Shepherd/Rottweiler mix with selectivity around dogs and unknown kid history meaningfully narrows adopter fit, suggesting a prolonged stay
• High story value combined with legitimate adoption complexity makes this the strongest candidate for a feature that drives real action

blurb:
Louise is three months old and weighs all of two and a half pounds, which means she could fit in a coat pocket and is also, objectively, a lot to handle in the best possible way.

She is still figuring out the whole trusting-people thing. She has been making progress, which is a good sign. Kittens who come in a little uncertain usually just need consistency and patience, and once they flip the switch, they flip it hard. Give Louise a calm environment and a little time, and she will get there.

She is already litter box trained, vaccinated, microchipped, and spayed. Her history with kids and other animals is not known yet, but the shelter is right there if you want to bring your household in for a meet and greet before committing. That is always a smart move with a kitten who is still warming up to the world.

Lewisville Animal Services is on College Pkwy in Lewisville. Walk in during visiting hours to meet her.
shelter_hours: Visit during shelter visiting hours — call ahead to confirm
scoring_notes:
• Tiny kitten appeal is high but her wariness around people narrows the ideal adopter pool considerably
• Backstory is thin with no known history, limiting the emotional hook a newsletter feature needs
• Recently arrived kitten with no indicators of extended wait time reduces urgency for readers

blurb:
Ten years old, a little pudgy, and completely unapologetic about both. Ethne is a domestic longhair who has clearly lived life on her own terms, and if you give her a quiet home to herself, she is going to reward you with all the affection she has been saving up.

She is litter box trained, vaccinated, microchipped, and already spayed. She loves people and is not shy about it. She does best as the only pet in the house, so if you are not running a multi-cat operation, that actually works in everyone's favor. No competition for the good spots on the couch. No drama at the food bowl. Just Ethne, doing her thing, probably sitting directly on whatever you are trying to read.

She could stand to lose a few ounces, so whoever adopts her gets the built-in purpose of being her wellness coach. Low stakes, high reward. Senior cats like Ethne often get overlooked, which is a real shame because they skip the chaotic kitten phase entirely and go straight to being good company.

Lewisville Animal Services is on College Pkwy in Lewisville. Stop in during visiting hours to meet her.
shelter_hours: Visit during shelter visiting hours — call ahead to confirm
scoring_notes:
• Senior cat with a fully charming, self-aware personality makes for an irresistible newsletter feature
• Built-in wellness coach angle gives adopters a fun sense of purpose and personal connection
• Ten-year-old cats are routinely overlooked, signaling a longer shelter stay and real urgency to act

blurb:
Taryn is four years old, about 34 pounds, and according to her foster, she is a calm, quiet girl who is a true companion dog for home. That's a direct quote. The foster also says she doesn't jump. For a Boxer mix with a reported energy level in the four-to-six range, that's saying something.

She went through the Prison Pups training program at Mostly Mutts and came out knowing a lot more than she did going in. She handled her bath and nail trim without drama. Fast movements or loud noises can startle her, but she recovers fast. She's a people dog at her core. Volunteers who spend time with her say she loves people more than just about anything.

With other dogs, she needed a few visits to warm up, but once she did, she was genuinely friendly. She did best with mellow females. She can be vocal when meeting dogs, especially from a distance, though that's been improving. She'd also be perfectly happy as your only dog. She met a couple of six-year-old boys at the rescue and did well, but kids ten and up would be the better fit, mostly because she doesn't like being hugged or feeling restrained, and younger kids don't always read that signal.

Head to mostlymutts.org to submit an inquiry or find out when you can come meet her in Kennesaw.

scoring_notes:
• Prison Pups graduate with a calm, people-first personality and a direct foster endorsement gives adopters rare, credible reassurance
• Moderate energy with no jumping in a Boxer mix is a legitimately surprising and sellable detail that cuts through typical rescue skepticism
• Multiple training program cycles and noted challenges with dog introductions suggest she has been in the system long enough to warrant featured placement

blurb:
Elana raised a whole litter of puppies named after Winter Olympics athletes. Every single one of them got adopted. Then she got adopted too, for a couple of weeks, before it didn't work out. Not her fault. Just wasn't the right fit. So now she's back, splitting time between two foster homes and waiting for her actual people to find her.

She's four years old, about 45 pounds, and has enough energy to wear out a younger dog on a slow day. She loves other dogs and has done well with every dog she's met across multiple foster homes and a short adoption. She makes growly noises when she plays, which sounds alarming but is just how she communicates. When she's in chill mode, she mostly ignores cats. When she's not in chill mode, she wants to play with them, which not every cat appreciates. So cats are a maybe, not a yes.

She's jumpy and mouthy when she gets excited, so kids in the home should be old enough to handle that kind of energy without getting knocked over. She liked the six-to-fourteen-year-old kids she met, and that range feels right.

If you have an active dog at home who's been looking for a real playmate, Elana might be the answer. Visit mostlymutts.org to start the inquiry process or find out when you can come meet her in Kennesaw.
shelter_hours: See mostlymutts.org for current adoption hours and appointment availability
scoring_notes:
• The angle of raising an entire adopted litter then being returned herself is a genuinely striking story that earns immediate reader sympathy
• High energy, multi-dog success record, and a clear adopter profile make her a strong match for active households with older kids
• A failed adoption plus an ongoing split between two foster homes signals meaningful time in limbo and real urgency to find her permanent home

blurb:
Roy has been through a lot for a nine-year-old. He showed up at animal control with thin fur, infected ears, sore eyes, and a mouth that needed serious dental work. Nobody knows how he got there. What's clear is that he came out the other side looking and feeling a whole lot better, and he's ready to spend whatever time he's got left being somebody's dog.

He went through the Mostly Mutts Prison Pups training program and learned plenty. In his foster home right now, he's respectful of an older chihuahua who wants nothing to do with him, friendly with the four cats (one of them actually seeks him out to cuddle), and calm around the eight-year-old boy he lives with. That's a pretty solid track record for a senior guy who had a rough go of it.

A couple of honest notes: Roy does best with kids who are old enough to read his cues and know not to hold food down at his level, since he may grab for it. No toddlers. If you have dogs or cats at home, a meet-and-greet first is the right call. But the foster home situation speaks for itself. This dog knows how to share a space.

Roy is at Mostly Mutts in Kennesaw. Check their website to start an inquiry or schedule a visit. He deserves a warm couch and someone who's going to take good care of him.
shelter_hours: See mostlymutts.org for current adoption hours and appointment availability
scoring_notes:
• Senior dog with a mystery past, serious medical history, and a full rehabilitation arc—the most emotionally compelling story in this batch
• Prison Pups training plus documented success with cats, dogs, and kids makes him more versatile than his age and needs might suggest
• Nine years old with an unknown prior history and medical baggage signals extended shelter exposure and the highest placement urgency of any candidate

blurb:
The volunteers named his litter after mixed nuts, and Cashew earned his name. While his siblings needed a little time to warm up when they arrived at the foster home, Cashew skipped that step entirely and went straight to having fun. Confident, constantly moving, and always looking for the next thing to climb. That's been his whole vibe from day one.

He's three to four months old and about three and a half pounds. Litter trained, no issues there. He loves wand toys, cat trees, and finding the highest spot in any room. When the energy runs out, he curls up in a soft bed and recharges. Then he does it all over again. He's currently living in the Kitty Room at Mostly Mutts with his siblings and getting plenty of attention from the shelter volunteers.

He got curious about the dogs in his foster home and did the classic kitten back-hunch. Not aggressive, just cautious. A patient, cat-savvy dog would probably be fine. He loves roughhousing with his siblings, so if you have another young cat at home who's up for a wrestling partner, Cashew is going to fit right in.

Mostly Mutts is in Marietta. Stop by the Kitty Room to meet him in person or reach out through their website to get the process started.
shelter_hours: Please check mostlymutts.org for current hours
scoring_notes:
• Highly adoptable kitten with zero behavioral flags and instant-on confidence that makes placement straightforward
• Whimsical mixed-nuts naming theme gives the newsletter a fun, shareable hook for readers
• Young, recently arrived, and still with siblings—low urgency compared to solo or longer-waiting candidates

blurb:
When Pistachio first arrived at her foster home, she needed some time. She was shy, unsure, taking everything in slowly. A few weeks of patience later and the real Pistachio showed up: calm, cuddly, and genuinely happy just to be close to her people. That's who she is now.

She's three to four months old, about three pounds, and fully litter trained. She loves wand toys, cat trees, and cozy beds. She'll play when the mood hits and cuddle when it doesn't. She's not going to demand your attention every second, but she does want to be near you. If you're looking for a low-drama companion who's sweet without being needy, that's Pistachio.

She grew up roughhousing with her siblings, so she's comfortable around other cats. She was curious about dogs in her foster home but did the cautious back-hunch, so a calm, cat-friendly dog would be worth a meet-and-greet before committing. Gentle kids would probably be fine too based on her temperament, though a meet first is always a good idea.

Pistachio is in the Kitty Room at Mostly Mutts in Marietta with her siblings. You can visit in person or reach out through their website to learn more about adopting her.
shelter_hours: Please check mostlymutts.org for current hours
scoring_notes:
• Low-drama temperament profile—calm, cuddly, not needy—speaks directly to a wide segment of adult and senior adopters
• Her shy-to-sweet transformation arc offers a brief but emotionally resonant story that newsletter readers will connect with

blurb:
Eight months old, five pounds, and already has a full comeback story. Kelly is a tortoiseshell kitten who was adopted once, had some litter box struggles in her first home, and got returned. Her foster took that problem seriously, dialed in her feeding schedule, and spent three weeks working through a food transition with her. Kelly has been using the litter box consistently ever since. That's not a red flag. That's a resolved issue with a documented fix.

She knows where her food is kept and exactly when it should arrive. When she's not playing, she's posted up at a window watching the neighborhood. Smart, curious, people-loving, and always wants to be in the middle of whatever you're doing. The volunteers describe her as a constant companion type, which checks out based on everything in her profile.

Kelly does well with gentle kids, got along with her siblings, and is interested in the cats in her current foster home. She also did fine with dogs in a previous placement, so a cat-friendly dog isn't a dealbreaker. The one thing to keep in mind: her feeding routine matters. Roughly half a cup of dry food twice a day keeps her litter box habits on track. Stick to that and you're good.

Mostly Mutts is in Kennesaw. You can reach out through their website to start the adoption process and arrange a meet.
shelter_hours: Please check mostlymutts.org for current hours
scoring_notes:
• Documented comeback story with a resolved litter box issue reframes a common adoption fear into a trust-builder
• Wide compatibility profile—kids, cats, and dogs—dramatically expands the pool of potential adopters
• A prior return plus three weeks of dedicated foster rehab signals meaningful time in the system and real urgency to place her

blurb:
Taryn's foster family calls her a true companion dog for home. That's not marketing language. That's a person who lives with her describing what she's actually like.

She's a four-year-old Boxer mix, about 34 pounds, and she came to Mostly Mutts through animal control. She went through the Prison Pups immersive training program and is now sitting in a foster home being calm, quiet, and good. She's not a jumper. She handled her bath and nail trim without drama. She loves people more than pretty much anything.

She does have opinions about other dogs, especially when she sees them from a distance or meets them for the first time. She can get vocal, and she warms up better over a few visits than she does all at once. Mellow female dogs tend to be her best matches. She'd also be fine as your only dog. Fast movements and loud noises can startle her, but she recovers quickly and doesn't hold a grudge. Kids around 10 and up are a good fit, and she's not into hugs, which honestly is a reasonable preference.

Taryn is at Mostly Mutts in Kennesaw. Submit an inquiry on their website or head in to meet her.
scoring_notes:
• Prison Pups graduate now thriving quietly in foster care is a ready-to-adopt, calm companion with broad adult-household appeal
• Foster family endorsement as a true home companion lends authentic credibility that resonates strongly with newsletter readers

blurb:
Elana raised a whole litter of puppies, all of them Winter Olympics themed, all of them adopted. She did her job. Now it's her turn.

She's a four-year-old Treeing Walker Coonhound mix, about 45 pounds, and she came into Mostly Mutts with her puppies after a kind person helped get them all to safety. She was adopted once already, but it wasn't the right fit, so she's back and splitting time between two foster homes while she waits for the right match. She loves other dogs, gets excited about pretty much every human she meets, and has energy to burn. The volunteers are not understating that part. She's mouthy and jumpy when she plays and makes growly sounds that are all enthusiasm and zero aggression.

Cats are a question mark. When she's calm, she ignores them. When she's in play mode, she's a lot for a cat to deal with. A dog-only home or a home with very confident cats would be the safer bet. Kids aged 10 and up are a better fit given her activity level.

If you have a yard and an active lifestyle and maybe already have a dog who wants a real playmate, Elana is worth meeting. She's at Mostly Mutts in Kennesaw.
scoring_notes:
• Winter Olympics litter backstory is an instant newsletter hook that practically writes its own headline
• Devoted mother returned after a failed adoption creates layered urgency and a deeply human-interest angle
• Two-foster-home arrangement and a prior failed adoption strongly indicate an above-average wait demanding reader action

blurb:
Roy has been through a lot. He showed up at animal control with thin fur, infected ears, sore eyes, and teeth that needed serious work. Nobody knows how he got there. But he's nine years old, he's a Bulldog-Shar Pei mix, and after all of that, he's still described as sweet and hopeful. That says something about a dog.

He went through the Mostly Mutts Prison Pups training program and graduated. He's living in a foster home right now where he respects the resident cats, gets along with other dogs, and hangs out calmly with the eight-year-old boy in the house. One of the cats even comes to snuggle with him. He's not trying to run the show. He just wants to be included.

A couple of things worth knowing: Roy does best with kids who are old enough to understand his cues and not hold food at his level, since he may accidentally nip chasing a snack. Older kids or adults-only homes are probably the best fit. He's about 46 pounds, fully vetted, and ready to go.

Roy is at Mostly Mutts in Kennesaw. You can start the process on their website or stop by to meet him in person.
scoring_notes:
• Senior dog with medical history and placement constraints narrows the pool but rewards the right reader with an extraordinary bond
• Arrival condition, Prison Pups graduation, and cat-snuggling detail compose one of the most compelling rescue arcs in this cohort
• Age, medical intake needs, and niche placement requirements signal an extended shelter journey making urgency undeniable

blurb:
Pistachio came in a little unsure of herself. New place, new people, a lot of unknowns. But she settled in, opened up, and landed on a personality that's pretty hard not to like. She's the cuddler of her litter. Once she's comfortable with you, she wants to be close.

She's three to four months old, around three pounds, and fully litter trained. She loves wand toys, climbing her cat tree, and wrestling with her siblings when the mood strikes. She's playful but not frantic about it. She'll match your energy pretty well, which is a nice quality in a kitten.

She does take a little time to warm up to new situations, so if you're looking for a cat that's immediately crawling all over guests, she might not be it. But if you want a cat that genuinely bonds with you and becomes your loyal little shadow, that's Pistachio. She does well with other cats and gentle kids, and could likely work with a calm dog depending on the individual animal.

She's currently at the Mostly Mutts Kitty Room in Marietta with her siblings. Visit mostlymutts.org to submit an adoption inquiry and go meet her.

blurb:
When Cashew and his siblings first arrived at their foster home, his brothers and sisters needed a little time to settle in. Cashew did not. He was ready to go from day one, climbing everything, chasing wands, and figuring out the highest spot in every room. The shelter describes him as the nuttiest one of the litter, and that tracks completely.

He loves wand toys, cat trees, and wrestling with his siblings. When he finally burns through his reserves, he'll curl up in a cozy bed and knock out. Rinse, repeat.

Cashew is currently in the Kitty Room at Mostly Mutts, soaking up attention from volunteers. Head to mostlymutts.org to submit an inquiry and set up a visit.

blurb:
This tortoiseshell kitten has already been around the block once. Kelly got adopted, had some litter box trouble in her previous home, and ended up back at Mostly Mutts. Not her fault. Her foster worked through the issue with her over a three-week stretch by adjusting her food portions and routine, and she's been solid ever since. She just needed a little structure, and now she's got it figured out.

She's eight months old, about five pounds, and very much a personality. She knows exactly where her food is kept and when it's supposed to show up. When she's not playing, she's posted up at a window watching the neighborhood do its thing. Smart, people-loving, and always ready to be in the middle of whatever you're doing.

Kelly does well with gentle kids, cat-friendly dogs, and other cats, so she's got flexibility most kittens don't. The one thing worth knowing: she does better with controlled portions, so you'll want to stick to the feeding routine her foster established. It's not complicated, just consistent. If that works for you, she's going to be a really easy cat to love.

Mostly Mutts is in Kennesaw. You can browse their adoptable cats and submit an inquiry through their website at mostlymutts.org.
